output.brief: Please don't send the breach notice on Friday. The data points away from Tessaly. Pelion's bags went through the same Tessaly crew pool and its rate didn't move. Corvane's rise sits entirely in bags diverted to the manual encode desk. Those bags were almost never mishandled before, but now about half of the encode-path bags miss their flights, and 91% reach the lateral after it closes. The diversions come from tags printed at Harlow Bay since 1 Sep on the new Fennick stock. Their no-read rate went from 1.5% to 11.8%. Transfer tags and Pelion tags are unchanged, so the airport's readers aren't the cause. Brackwater tags printed on the same counters during the 14–16 Oct shortage read at 1.6%, while kiosk tags printed the same days on Fennick stock failed at 12%. The added evening flights aren't the driver. What to do next: switch counters and kiosks back to the Brackwater stock held in stores now, and watch the no-read rate and mishandling rate. Test the Fennick stock against the printer heat settings separately. That will show whether the stock is defective or just mismatched, so hold off on a defect claim until then. Asking the airport for an extra encode workstation in the evening is a reasonable stopgap. Confidence is high on the tag-stock cause and moderate on whether the stock or the printer settings are at fault.
